title: Frontend: Grid Lights
businessContext: Build and verify the core behavior behind Grid Lights. This independently authored exercise has a bounded, explicit contract. Injected clock, network, random, or worker models are identified in the contract; they do not claim production service guarantees.
problemStatement: Export App. Four buttons[data-cell=0..3] form a light grid. Pressed state matches active membership; output[data-testid=count] is active count. Each click toggles that cell independently. Phase output remains ready.
constraints: Export default App. Only react and react/jsx-runtime imports are supported. The DOM contract and supplied props define the exercise.
Preserve identity, ordering, boundary behavior, and error messages stated in the contract. Passing fixtures verifies this contract, not every production concern.
candidateTasks: Implement the documented behavior without hard-coding fixture answers.
Run the full suite, investigate boundary failures, and explain the follow-up variation.
hints: Write down the state or algorithmic invariant, and trace the smallest boundary case before coding.
Represent active cells by stable coordinates or IDs and derive the count.
alternativeApproaches: Add a neighborhood-toggle puzzle and specify whether invalid cells or repeated events are ignored.
commonMistakes: Ignoring contract boundaries such as: Toggle twice; all on/off; changing grid dimensions.
Treating a local deterministic model as proof of durable storage, authorization, distributed coordination, or physical-world guarantees.
